copy.blurb:
A +24.1pp gap on the Curaçao side. Ecuador v Curaçao in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Curaçao stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Public Elo rates Ecuador 20 points higher than the other side (Ecuador 1810, Curaçao 1790). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Ecuador to win at 38%, the draw at 29%, and Curaçao to win at 34%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Curaçao on the win side reads 34%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Ecuador to win at 78%, the draw at 14%, and Curaçao to win at 9%. The Curaçao side trades at 9% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +958. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 34%, +24.1pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Curaçao side that lower bound is 28% — +19.0pp clear of the market's 9%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Curaçao side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 33 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Curaçao a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +24.1pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model thinks Curaçao are mispriced. Our number reads 34% on the away side; the market reads 9%. The +24.1pp gap is the Pick.
